family.name: Financial Analyst (FP&A)
family.summary: Profit beat the budget, so the CEO is happy, but revenue missed: split the miss into price and volume, see that the cost savings are only timing, reforecast the year, and catch the errors in a junior’s reforecast.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Was it really a good quarter?
stages.summary: Explain a profit beat that hides a revenue miss: split price and volume, and see the cost savings are timing. Think aloud.

stages.title: Reforecast the year
stages.summary: Choose how to reforecast after the quarter. Tests forecasting judgement. Think aloud.

stages.title: The CFO and CEO react
stages.summary: Pushback on their reforecast. Tests holding a position with numbers.

stages.title: Check a junior's reforecast
stages.summary: A reforecast that annualises a quarter with a one-off deal in it, mislabels a variance and drops the delayed costs. Think aloud.

stages.title: Board pack commentary (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the quarter commentary for the board pack with AI. Catches spin and arithmetic errors.

stages.title: A forecast that missed
stages.summary: A real forecast or budget that turned out wrong. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the FP&A analyst at **Pulse Fitness**, which sells gym memberships across 30 centres. Q1 has just closed. The CEO says: "Profit beat the budget, great quarter." The CFO asks you for the real story before the board pack goes out.

brief.caption: Q1: budget against actual (₹ lakh)
rows: EBITDA (profit before interest, tax and depreciation)

items: Sales ran a 9% launch offer all quarter to hit unit targets.
9 budgeted hires joined two months late; they are all on board now.
Marketing paused two campaigns while the agency was replaced; the new agency starts next month with the full budget.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: How would you explain "profit" versus "cash" to a friend?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: Was it really a good quarter?

prompt.text: **Explain the quarter to the CFO in numbers.** Why did revenue miss, why did profit beat, and will the beat last?

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Keep the annual budget; assume the shortfall is caught up later in the year
Cut the revenue forecast to the current run rate and keep costs as budgeted
Cut revenue to the run rate and move the delayed hiring and marketing into later quarters
Show the CFO three scenarios (low, base, high) instead of one number

prompt.text: **How do you reforecast the rest of the year?** Pick one, show roughly what it does to annual revenue and profit, and say what you're assuming about the discount.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep the annual budget; assume the shortfall is caught up later in the year"

prompt.text: Next quarter, the discount continued, the hires were paid in full and the new agency spent its whole budget. Profit missed the budget badly. The CFO asks why the forecast didn't warn them.
**What do you say and do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Cut the revenue forecast to the current run rate and keep costs as budgeted"

prompt.text: The CEO looks at your forecast: "Revenue is down but costs are the same, so profit collapses? That's too gloomy for the board." The CFO asks you to check it.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Cut revenue to the run rate and move the delayed hiring and marketing into later quarters"

prompt.text: The Sales head insists the 9% offer ends this month and prices will recover fully, so your revenue cut is "too pessimistic". The CEO wants to use the Sales view.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Show the CFO three scenarios (low, base, high) instead of one number"

prompt.text: The CFO says: "Three numbers confuse the board. Which one do I present?" The low and high cases are far apart.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior analyst sends you this reforecast summary. **Find the errors, worst first, and say how much each one throws the forecast off.**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Full-year revenue = this quarter's revenue × 4 = 1,264. (This quarter included a one-off bulk order of 17.4.)
Full-year payroll = this quarter's payroll × 4 = 364.
Revenue variance this quarter: -31, shown as **favourable**.
Marketing for the rest of the year kept at this quarter's level.
Source: the ledger as of the close date; reviewed by the controller.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the commentary for the board pack (under 180 words): revenue against budget and why, profit against budget and why, and what it means for the rest of the year.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a forecast or budget you worked on that turned out wrong.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
